subtopic: Friendship betrayal to reconciliation or ending
subtype: Stage 4: Anger, retaliation urge and withdrawal [Receiver]
passage:
I'm Nathan, Elizabeth's older brother, and I've never seen her the way she was on Tuesday. She came home, dropped her bag in the hallway and went straight to her laptop. When I looked over her shoulder, she was typing a post about Anjali, something about Anjali's mum and the shop. Her jaw was tight and her hands were quick.
"She told everyone about me," she said without looking up. "So now everyone gets to know about her."
I don't know everything that happened between them. I just said, "Lizzie, can you wait till tomorrow? Right now you're the one who got hurt. Post that and you're the one who did the hurting."
She glared at me. Then she deleted the draft, blocked Anjali's number instead, and lay face-down on the sofa for an hour. I made her toast. I can't tell if she's angry or just really sad.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth do instead of posting?
qa.a: Elizabeth deleted the draft and blocked Anjali's number instead.

qa.q: Why did Elizabeth want to post about Anjali?
qa.a: Elizabeth was furious that Anjali told everyone about her and wanted Anjali to feel the same exposure.

qa.q: Why was waiting a day a wise suggestion?
qa.a: Anger that strong usually cools a little overnight; posting Anjali's secret would have made Elizabeth the one who did harm, while waiting keeps her choices open.

qa.q: How does Nathan see Elizabeth's evening?
qa.a: Nathan sees how upset his sister is but can't tell whether she is angry or deeply sad, so he stays near and makes her toast.

grounding: Shows a hurt teenage girl wanting to expose her friend's secret or cut her off, and a brother urging her to wait a day so she does not become the wrongdoer.

subtopic: Friendship betrayal to reconciliation or ending
subtype: Stage 4: Anger, retaliation urge and withdrawal [Receiver]
passage:
Monday: Urmila found out at lunch that Darshan had told the whole cricket group she still sleeps with a night lamp and hid in the storeroom during the last thunderstorm. By evening she had typed a message to the class group about Darshan's report card, the one his father tore up. Her thumb hovered over send.
Tuesday: She hadn't sent it. Her cousin Manu had said, "Sleep on it. If it's still right tomorrow, it'll still be right." In class she moved to the front bench and didn't look back once when Darshan said "Urmi". She felt cold, as if a door had slammed shut inside her.
Friday: The anger had cooled into something heavier. She deleted the draft. She still wasn't talking to Darshan. But she was glad the story about the report card was still his to tell.

qa.q: What did Darshan tell the cricket group about Urmila?
qa.a: Darshan told them she still sleeps with a night lamp and hid in the storeroom during the last thunderstorm.

qa.q: How was Urmila feeling on Tuesday, and what shows it?
qa.a: Urmila felt cold and shut off; she moved to the front bench and didn't look back when Darshan called her 'Urmi'.

qa.q: How did waiting help Urmila avoid a mistake?
qa.a: Sleeping on it let the anger cool, so Urmila deleted the draft instead of exposing Darshan's secret and becoming the one in the wrong.

qa.q: What would change for Darshan if Urmila had sent the message on Monday?
qa.a: Darshan's private pain about the report card would have been exposed, and the story would shift from what Darshan did to what Urmila did.

grounding: Illustrates a teen's urge to retaliate by exposing a friend's secret and her withdrawal, with waiting a day keeping her on the right side of the story.
